title: Multi-omics and machine learning nominate ADAM9 as a driver gene in severe COVID-19
summary: In a cohort of people under 50 without major comorbidities (47 critical, 25 non-critical COVID-19 patients and 22 healthy individuals), an ensemble of machine learning, deep learning, quantum annealing and structural causal modeling identified a gene signature separating critical from non-critical patients, with upregulated ADAM9 as a key driver. The signature was replicated in an independent cohort of 81 critical and 73 recovered patients, and ex vivo ADAM9 inhibition affected SARS-CoV-2 uptake and replication in human lung epithelial cells. The discovery cohort is small and this is a preprint (2021-06-25).
ai_technology: Ensemble of machine learning, deep learning, quantum annealing and structural causal modeling on multi-omics data
organization: Universite de Strasbourg (INSERM UMR_S 1109); Nouvel Hopital Civil, Strasbourg

evidence.tested: Replication of the signature in an independent cohort of 81 critical and 73 recovered patients; ex vivo ADAM9 inhibition in human lung epithelial cells.
evidence.unknown: Clinical benefit of targeting ADAM9 is not shown; abstract-level review; the contribution of each AI component to the finding is not separable from the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble machine learning, deep learning, quantum annealing and causal modeling analyzed multi-omics data to identify driver genes.
